name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
description: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva and the holiest of all Shiva temples. Situated on the western bank of the Ganga in Varanasi, the eternal city. The current temple was built by Ahilya Bai Holkar in 1780. The Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, inaugurated in 2021, connects the temple directly to the Ganga.
significance: Kashi itself is the body of Shiva. Whoever dies in Kashi attains Moksha — Shiva whispers the Taraka Mantra in the dying person's ear. The Jyotirlinga here is the cosmic pillar of light from which Shiva revealed his infinite nature.
howToReach: Varanasi (Lal Bahadur Shastri Airport, 25km). Temple is in Vishwanath Gali — accessible on foot from Godowlia Crossing or via the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor from Manikarnika Ghat.
bestTime: October to March. Maha Shivaratri draws lakhs of pilgrims.

name: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir
description: The newly consecrated Ram Mandir at the birthplace of Shri Ram in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh. Consecrated in January 2024, this nagara-style temple is built with Rajasthan's pink sandstone and represents the fulfilment of a centuries-old aspiration of the Hindu world.
significance: Ayodhya is the birthplace of Maryada Purushottam Ram — the ideal king, ideal son, and ideal husband. This is the most significant temple consecration in modern Hindu history.
howToReach: Ayodhya has its own Maharishi Valmiki International Airport. Also accessible by train (Ayodhya Cantt or Ayodhya Junction) from Lucknow (130km) or Varanasi (200km).
bestTime: Ram Navami (March-April) and Diwali (October-November) are peak spiritual seasons.

name: Jagannath Temple
description: One of the four sacred Char Dhams of Hindu pilgrimage. The 12th century temple stands 65 metres tall and houses the wooden idols of Jagannath (Vishnu), Balabhadra (his brother), and Subhadra (his sister). The Mahaprasad offered here is considered sacred across the world.
significance: Puri is one of the four Dhamas — the abodes of God at the four cardinal directions. The Rath Yatra here, observed for over 2,000 years, is the world's largest chariot procession.
howToReach: Bhubaneswar Airport (65km from Puri). Puri has its own railway station with connections to major cities. The temple is in the heart of Puri town.
bestTime: Rath Yatra (June-July) is the most significant time. Winter months are pleasant for darshan.

name: Tirupati Balaji (Tirumala)
description: The richest and most visited religious site in the world, receiving over 50,000 pilgrims daily. Lord Venkateswara (Balaji) resides on the seven hills of Tirumala. The temple is managed by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD).
significance: Venkateswara is believed to fulfill all sincere wishes. The tradition of offering hair (tonsure) to Balaji as gratitude is practiced by millions each year.
howToReach: Tirupati Airport. Trains to Tirupati from Chennai (130km), Bangalore (275km). Buses from Tirupati to Tirumala (19km hill road) or cable car.
bestTime: Brahmotsavam (September-October) — 9-day grand festival. Avoid peak weekends if possible.

name: Kedarnath Temple
description: At 3,583 metres in the Himalayas, Kedarnath is the highest Jyotirlinga and one of the Char Dhams. The temple is believed to have been built by the Pandavas and reconstructed by Adi Shankaracharya. The temple opens only for 6 months every year (May–November).
significance: Kedarnath is where Lord Shiva appeared as a buffalo to escape the Pandavas. Worshipping here absolves all sins. Adi Shankaracharya attained Mahasamadhi here at age 32.
howToReach: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (247km). By road to Gaurikund, then 16km trek or helicopter. Helicopter service from Phata, Sitapur, or Guptkashi.
bestTime: May-June (right after opening) or September-October (before closing). Summer is ideal.

name: Badrinath Temple
description: One of the 108 Divya Desams and part of the Chota Char Dham. Situated at 3,133 metres between the Nar and Narayan mountain ranges. The idol of Badri Narayan is made of shaligram stone and is considered one of the most ancient self-manifested deities.
significance: Adi Shankaracharya discovered the idol in the Alaknanda River and installed it here. The Vishnu Puranam declares — 'In the Kali age, none is saved without visiting Badrinath.'
howToReach: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (320km). Nearest railhead is Haridwar (295km). Road journey from Haridwar or Rishikesh, passing through Joshimath.
bestTime: May-June and September-October. The temple is open for approximately 6 months annually.

name: Shri Vaishno Devi Mandir
description: One of the most sacred Shakti Peethas, receiving over 8 million pilgrims annually — the second-most visited religious site in the world. The Goddess manifests as three natural rock formations (Pindis) representing Mahakali, Mahalakshmi, and Mahasaraswati in a mountain cave at 5,200 feet.
significance: The three Pindis of the Goddess exist in their natural form since time immemorial. A pilgrimage to Vaishno Devi is considered complete only when the Devi herself calls you.
howToReach: Jammu Airport (50km to Katra). Jammu Tawi station, then bus/taxi to Katra. From Katra, 14km trek to the holy cave or helicopter to Sanjhichhat.
bestTime: March-May and October-November. Navratri (both Chaitra and Sharad) sees peak pilgrimage.

name: Somnath Temple
description: The first and foremost Jyotirlinga — Somnath is called the 'Eternal Shrine' (Prabhasa Tirtha). The present temple, rebuilt in 1951 under Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's leadership, stands on the Arabian Sea coast in Saurashtra. The sea-facing lingam is at the precise tip of India.
significance: Somnath has been destroyed and rebuilt seven times — its resilience symbolises the indestructibility of faith. The arrow shaft on the seaward wall points south in a straight line — no land till Antarctica.
howToReach: Diu Airport (65km) or Keshod Airport (55km). Nearest railway is Veraval (7km). Well-connected by road from Junagadh (85km) and Rajkot (195km).
bestTime: October to March. Maha Shivaratri sees enormous crowds.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
description: One of the most magnificent temples in India — a living city within a city. The 14 gopurams (gateway towers) are covered with thousands of painted stucco figures. The temple complex covers 14 acres and is over 2,500 years old in its origins.
significance: Meenakshi is Parvati who was born in Madurai as the daughter of the Pandya king. Her divine wedding with Shiva (as Sundareshwar) is re-enacted every year in the grand Chithirai Festival.
howToReach: Madurai Airport (12km from temple). Madurai Junction railway station is 2km from the temple. Well-connected by road from Chennai (450km) and Coimbatore (200km).
bestTime: Chithirai Festival (April-May). January-March is pleasant weather.

name: Siddhivinayak Temple
description: One of the most visited and revered Ganesha temples in India, located in Prabhadevi, Mumbai. The idol of Siddhivinayak (the wish-fulfilling Ganesha) has a unique left-curved trunk — a rare and especially powerful form. Built in 1801, the temple receives over 100,000 devotees on Tuesdays.
significance: Siddhivinayak is believed to fulfill all desires of sincere devotees. The word 'Siddhi' means fulfilment of wishes. Celebrities, politicians, and common people alike visit every Tuesday.
howToReach: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (12km). Dadar station (2km) — both Central and Western line. Well-connected by bus and local train.
bestTime: Tuesdays are most auspicious. Ganesh Chaturthi sees extraordinary celebrations.

name: Dwarkadhish Temple
description: One of the four sacred Char Dhams. The Jagat Mandir or Dwarkadhish temple stands on the northern bank of the Gomati River, near where it meets the Arabian Sea. The 5-storey temple tower rises 51.8 metres. Dwarka was the capital of Krishna's kingdom.
significance: Dwarka is where Krishna ruled as king after leaving Mathura. The city is believed to have been built in a single night by Vishwakarma. The ancient city is said to be submerged under the sea.
howToReach: Jamnagar Airport (137km). Dwarka Railway Station — connected to Ahmedabad (450km) and Mumbai. Well-connected by bus from Rajkot (250km) and Jamnagar.
bestTime: November to February. Janmashtami (August) is the peak festival season.
